content: The test image shows a collapsed/dead seedling at soil level — the plant has damped off, with surrounding healthy green seedlings. This is classic damping-off. Top candidates: Pythium_damping_off, Rhizoctonia, Phytophthora.

Based on my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Single completely collapsed/dead seedling at soil surface level
- Tan/yellow coloring of the stem — appears dried and dead
- Sandy/dry soil conditions
- Surrounding plants (trifoliate-stage soybean seedlings) are healthy green
- Classic post-emergence damping-off pattern

**Reference image comparison:**
- **Rhizoctonia**: Bottom-right panel shows collapsed seedlings in sandy soil — very similar field scene to the test image
- **Pythium_damping_off**: Shows very early-stage (cotyledon) seedlings with water-soaked/soft rot symptoms in darker, wetter soil conditions — less matching
- **Phytophthora**: Shows more mature plants with yellowing and brown stem discoloration extending up several nodes — not matching

The collapsed seedling in dry sandy soil with neighboring healthy plants is most consistent with Rhizoctonia post-emergence damping-off. Pythium typically occurs in wet/saturated soils and at an earlier seedling stage with water-soaked soft rot. The dry sandy conditions and the stage of the collapsed plant better fit Rhizoctonia.
